I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked for me last year, then I adjust a little if the weather, prices, or seed look different. I have 7 mu, not a huge area, so I still count every bag of fertilizer and every irrigation fee, but I do not dare save too much on fertilizer and lose yield. Around Quzhou, for wheat-maize land with well water, I will keep the full 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, not old saved seed, because the newer ones usually stand better and fill grain better if I manage water on time. I will put a solid base fertilizer before sowing, mainly nitrogen with phosphorus, and a smaller amount of potassium. Then I will topdress once at jointing. For water, I will not be stingy if the soil is dry: one winter or freezing water if needed, one at jointing, one at filling, so about 3 times in a normal year. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives yield here if the stand is even. I will return some straw if it is chopped fine, but I will still feed fertilizer because maize pulls a lot. I will put part of the nitrogen at sowing and the rest before the big bell-mouth stage, with enough phosphorus and some potassium. For maize I will usually water 2 times with my well, once after sowing if dry and once around big flare or tasseling. For pests and disease, I do not spray by calendar only, but in a normal year I will end up spraying wheat 2 times and maize 2 times. I will use rotary tillage after maize for wheat sowing because it is quicker on my 7 mu and common here, and I will use no-tillage maize seeding after wheat if the machine is available, since it saves time in the tight wheat-maize changeover. If weather is normal, I will aim around 500 kg per mu for wheat and 600 kg per mu for maize. That is the kind of target worth spending for on my land and with my well water.
